LimitsOut.description:
Used against allowed, so the screen can warn before a 429. A user with
their own key (`has_own_key`) does not spend the default key.
LimitsOut.title: LimitsOut

PendingOut.description: What a person is asked to approve, so the screen needs no step parsing.
PendingOut.title: PendingOut

get.description:
What is left before a limit: asks on the shared default key today, unfinished
runs against the cap, whether you saved your own key, and open live streams.
Read only.

Your runs, newest first unless `ordering` says otherwise (`created_at` or
`latency_ms`, `-` for descending). Filter by `status` (repeat it for several),
`q` (text in the question) and `created_after` / `created_before`. `meta.count`
is the number of runs that match.

post.description:
Start a run. The agent plans and proposes SQL, then waits for approval; follow
it on `/runs/{id}/events`. One run counts as one spend of the shared default key.

get.description: A run and its steps. Poll this when the live stream is not available.

post.description: Run the SQL the agent proposed. Only while the run waits for approval.
End a paused run without running anything.

Run your own SQL instead. It goes through the same guard; a refusal is a 400
and the run stays paused.

get.description:
Server-sent events: `step` for each step, then one `status` event when the
run pauses for approval or ends. Event ids are step indexes; reconnect with
`Last-Event-ID` to continue. Over the open-stream limit it answers 429
`agent_stream_limit`: poll `GET /runs/{id}` instead.

The stored trace in order. No model call and no query on the demo database:
it is read from the steps alone.

The rows of a succeeded run, up to the row cap. Rows are not stored: this
runs the run's stored SQL again, through the guard, on the read-only
connection. It never takes SQL from the request, so the numbers can differ
from the first run if the data changed. 409 `run_not_succeeded` otherwise.

post.description:
Answer a question about the demo database: the SQL that ran, the result
table and a confidence score. The SQL is checked before it runs and runs on
the read-only connection only.

get.description:
Every dependency the backend needs. Not wrapped in the envelope, so
uptime checks can read `status` directly; 503 when anything fails.

The signed-in user's saved keys: provider, last four characters, model.
The key itself is never returned.

put.description: Check the key with the provider and save it encrypted.

get.description:
The signed-in user, or 401. The frontend's route guards use this.

Also sets the csrftoken cookie (signed in or not): the app calls this
first on every load, so its first POST already has a token to send.

Every table of the demo schema with columns, keys, comments and row
estimates. Send `If-None-Match` with the last `ETag` to get a 304 when
nothing changed.

One table, same shape as in the full schema. An unknown name is a 404
`table_not_found` that says nothing else about the schema.
